description: A sixteen channel gate sequencer with sixteen straight steps, twelve triplet steps, sixteen stored patterns, four working modes and its own clock

params.text: In pattern mode this turns the selected channel on or off for that step; in sequence mode it sets the pattern number; in mute mode it mutes its own output; in now mode it plays its output while held
In pattern mode this turns the selected channel on or off for that triplet step; in the other three modes it chooses which of three pattern slots its quarter of the bar uses
Starts and stops the sequencer; its lamp blinks with the beat rather than showing whether the sequencer is running
Sets the sequencer back to the start of its 64 beat cycle; its lamp lights through the first beat of that cycle
Sets the tempo, 0 to 240 beats per minute
Puts the module into pattern mode, where the step buttons set the pattern of the selected channel
Puts the module into sequence mode, where the step buttons choose which pattern number each quarter of the bar plays
Puts the module into mute mode, where each of the sixteen step buttons mutes its own output
Puts the module into now mode, where holding a step button plays its output straight away and makes it the channel being edited
Sets the gate length as a fraction of a step, 0 to 100 per cent, which also sets the width of the run and reset outputs
Stores the pattern and channel playing now as the source for the paste button, and lights while that stored pattern is the one playing
Copies the stored pattern over the one playing: one channel in pattern mode and all sixteen in the other modes, lighting while the stored channel matches the one selected
Bends the timing of the triplet steps, pushing them early at fully counter-clockwise and late fully clockwise
Bends the timing of the straight steps, pushing them early at fully counter-clockwise and late fully clockwise

inputs.text: A pitch naming one of the module's buttons, read whenever the gate input goes high; C2 to B5 covers the whole panel
Presses the button the CV input names, on each rising edge above 2V
Scrolls the play position through the 64 beat cycle, the whole cycle over 10V

outputs.text: 10V while that channel's step is on and the gate length has not run out, and 0V otherwise; a muted channel carries 0V
10V for the part of every beat the gate length knob sets, as a clock for other modules
10V for the part of the first beat of the 64 beat cycle the gate length knob sets, as a reset for other modules

notes: the sequencer comes up stopped: nothing moves until the run button is pressed
there is no clock input; the module runs from its own tempo knob, and the position input is the only way to move it from outside
every output is set to one channel whatever is patched in, so the module is monophonic
which of the sixteen patterns plays is chosen a quarter of a bar at a time, through three slots per quarter that the triplet buttons switch between in sequence mode
the patterns are saved with the patch, and so are the mode, the mutes, the selected channel and the run state, which are parameters with no control on the panel

inputs.0:
1V per octave · stepped · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.1:
high above 2V · stepped · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
